question: In which of the following parts of the human body do the epithelial cells have cilia?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Respiratory tract**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ciliated epithelial cells** are specialized **epithelial cells** that possess hair-like protoplasmic outgrowths called **cilia** on their free surface.
 
• In the **human body**, these cells are primarily located in the **Respiratory tract**, including the **nasal passages**, **trachea** (windpipe), and **bronchi**.
 
• The main **function** of the cilia in the **respiratory system** is to move **mucus**, **dust**, and **pathogens** away from the **lungs** and toward the **throat**, where they can be swallowed or expelled.
 
• This rhythmic, wave-like motion is essential for the **mucociliary clearance** mechanism, which serves as a primary defense against **respiratory infections**. ***Hence, the respiratory tract is the correct answer.***
 
• These cells are usually **columnar** or **cuboidal** in shape and are anchored to a **basement membrane**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Buccal Cavity:**
 
 
• The **buccal cavity** (mouth) is lined with **Non-keratinized Stratified Squamous Epithelium**.
 
• This tissue consists of multiple layers of cells designed to protect the underlying structures from **mechanical stress** and **abrasion** caused by **chewing**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Food Pipe (Esophagus):**
 
 
• The **esophagus** is also lined with **non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium**.
 
• The primary role of the **epithelium** here is to provide a smooth surface for the passage of the **bolus** and to protect against the friction of **food particles**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Stomach Wall:**
 
 
• The **stomach wall** is lined with **Simple Columnar Epithelium**.
 
• These cells are specialized for **secretion** and **protection**; they secrete **mucus** to protect the stomach lining from **hydrochloric acid (HCl)** and **digestive enzymes** like **pepsin**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Fallopian Tubes:**
 
 
• Besides the **respiratory tract**, **ciliated epithelium** is also found in the **oviducts** (**Fallopian tubes**) of the **female reproductive system**.
 
• In this **location**, the cilia help in the transport of the **ovum** (egg) from the **ovary** toward the **uterus**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between Cilia and Microvilli:**
 
 
• **Cilia** are involved in **movement** and transport of substances across the cell surface, whereas **microvilli** (found in the **small intestine**) are primarily for increasing the **surface area** for **absorption**.
 
 
 
• **Clinical Significance:**
 
 
• A **genetic disorder** known as **Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia** (**PCD**) or **Kartagener Syndrome** occurs when the cilia fail to move correctly, leading to chronic **sinusitis**, **bronchitis**, and **infertility**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Epithelium:**
 
 
• **Squamous:** Thin, flat cells (e.g., **alveoli** of lungs).
 
• **Cuboidal:** Cube-like cells (e.g., **kidney tubules**).
 
• **Columnar:** Tall, pillar-like cells (e.g., **intestine**).
